author: reasoning-proposal-agent
title: Current reasoning strategies (2026-10-01 reading)
body: reference = bounded JS (function-free Horn with explicit negation as independent evidence, finite Int constraints by enumeration, JS controllers for abduce/diagnose/plan/simulate/induce/analogize). advanced = the same JS plus optional SWI-Prolog (point-in-time Horn closure only; JS rebuilds the proof and checks agreement) and Z3 (QF_LIA constraints and optimisation; not a Horn backend). Missing: negation as failure, aggregates beyond host counting, defaults, tabling and magic sets, incremental indexing, a partial-answer protocol richer than maxNodes/timeout flags. The contract is spread over DS006, DS013, wire help pages and registry.mjs comments, hence the confusing feeling.

author: reasoning-proposal-agent
title: advanced_research.md is a VRC roadmap, not a strategy catalogue
body: The 48 cards R01-R48 (groups A-H, stages 0-4, priorities P0-P3) are all PLANNED research directions for VRC (verified representation compilation, bounded planning, dreaming registry). SWI tabling, Soufflé, CSP/SMT, external planners and abductive solvers appear only as comparators (mainly R02, R27, R38, R42). No card covers top-down tabling, bottom-up Datalog, SAT/SMT/CP, ASP or argumentation as strategies. The proposal therefore (a) reuses the cards that are strategy-neutral (R01 pilot, R02 fair comparison and attribution, R03 selector, R05 metamorphic audit, R18 batching/demand, R21-R27 semantic extensions, R28 dreaming budget, R47 epistemic status, R46 NL ingestion), and (b) adds its own comparison matrix across strategy families.

author: reasoning-proposal-agent
title: Zip evidence summary (what is validated and what is not)
body: Run as plain Node here: soplab (23/23 tests), sop-r (difftest 5100/5100, grade-compound), E10 (202/202 tests, 20/20 regressions), VRC (113/113 tests). NOT validated anywhere: comparison with SWI-Prolog or Soufflé (VRC skipped all 9, E10 never tried), any default/defeasible reasoning, ASP, SMT beyond the existing Z3 adapter, natural-language ingestion at real-text scale (sop-r pilot used a 980-word fictional handbook; LLM reading the text directly also scored 144/144). Scale evidence is synthetic (sop-r 100k entities, E10 1M-fact ring components, VRC 1M background facts).

author: reasoning-proposal-agent
title: Proposal: core wires plus sugar, capability-declared strategies, router, retrieval guard
body: Unified wire set: core (predicate, fact, rule with not and absent, compare, compute, aggregate, constraint, action, goal, hypothesis, policy) plus sugar (default, integrity desugar to stratified NAF rules) plus method; query surface unchanged plus modes why_not, plan, abduce. Strategies are separate and declare capabilities; unsupported means not expressible, never weakened. Router: rules first, then portfolio, then learned (literature: Rice, SATzilla, MachSMT, AutoFolio, Delfi; E10 neural ranker only tied the heuristic). Retrieval at scale: symbol-driven slice plus targeted widening, and the rule that NAF, aggregates, count and every are valid only over closed and fully retrieved predicates.

author: reasoning-proposal-agent
title: Smoke harness results (39 cases, five strategies)
body: js-reference 28/28 (11 not expressible), prolog-swi 21/21 (18), z3-lia 3/3 (36), datalog-e10 22/22 (17), datalog-soplab 28/29 (10; fail = abduce returns one cheapest explanation). No engine passes 06d (compute in rules), 11c (method), 13b (why-not). Retrieval cases 20-22: targeted widening retrieved 5/9305, 4/3904 and 9/2009 wires with 100% recall of needed wires; guard disabled gives wrong answers in all three. Product parser refuses slices over 2048 wires.

author: proposal-revision-agent
title: Round 2: both is paraconsistent, blocking is by fire, strict contrary blocks defaults
body: Chose Belnap-style independent positive and negative evidence (both is a reported status, R-P1 holds) over blocking propagation. Defaults block by fire; overrides is the composable form and priority compiles to it; a strict contrary (explicit negative fact or a rule not depending on defaults) blocks a default automatically, the Nixon diamond stays both. Evidence: smoke cases 09b, 09d, 09e pass on E10 and soplab after desugaring.

author: proposal-revision-agent
title: Completion in Z3 is unsound for recursion (run with the private Z3)
body: eval/smoke-reasoning/probes/z3-04b-completion-recursion.smt2: with edges a-b, b-a and an isolated c, the completion of reach has a model with reach(a,c) (sat), although reach(a,c) is not derivable. z3-smt-bounded therefore declares recursion unsupported; 09a passed in round 1 only because it has no recursion. The 09a two-relation lowering probe returns unsat unsat unsat.

author: proposal-r3-agent
title: Reasoning wires proposal, round 3 (review round 2 applied)
body: Round 3 of experiments/proposal/reasoning-wires-proposal.md applies the reviewer's round-2 report (verdict: ready after minor fixes). MUST 1: default conclusions are completeness-sensitive (retrieval completeness for the strict contrary and exception keys; R-P1 judged on the desugared program; case 24, with the guard off the first answer tweety+pingu is accepted and wrong). MUST 2: conditional per row and verified by a run on observed facts plus the leave-one-out set; otherwise all assumptions with conditional_unknown (case 10f, the a/b/c counterexample). MUST 3: used is one sufficient support set; host deletion verified by replay, else used_incomplete; the comparator replays used in the oracle (cases 13c, 13d). MUST 4: ASP integrity exception removed. SHOULD 1-9 applied (obligation triggers and qualifier table, severity x binding matrix, scope matching, contested binds flagged, conform with time and lowering to core rules, blocked_by in ASP/Z3, interval combination table, governance on action, housekeeping). New: experiments/proposal/wire-authoring-guide.md (grammar generated by validator.mjs --grammar-compact; every example validated). Appendices E (inventory), F (smoke results) and G (declared coverage, a declaration not a prediction) take the three big tables. Smoke: 79 cases (10 new), 56 invalid fixtures, 23 comparator checks; js-reference 35/35, prolog-swi 28/28, z3-lia 3/3, datalog-e10 37/37, datalog-soplab 43/44 (the known abduce finding), js-oracle 59/59 (oracle-agent's adapter, concurrent). author: oracle-agent
title: js-reference oracle built: 59 of 59 declared smoke cases pass
body: The JavaScript oracle of the proposed core is implemented in reasoning/strategies/js-reference/ beside the reference and advanced routes (owner approval 2026-10-01; other strategies, sop/ grammar moves and routing wait for the review). Smoke column js-oracle: pass 59, fail 0, not expressible 20 (modes of work, declared). The hand-derived expected answers (01b, 06d, 07b, 07c, 12c-12f, 13b) were all reproduced, so no expected file was changed. Cross-check against the other live adapters (138 pairs where both pass): 132 identical packets; 6 differences are cosmetic or legitimate (rows on count, a different sound subset of rows after a round or probe cut). Design choices fixed where the proposal was open: why_not uses existing evidence first and grounds free variables over the slice constants only when nothing matches (nearest explanation); a count has no rows; an every whose scope atom has both P and N is both; partial positive answers after a budget cut only for programs with no NAF or aggregate; conditional is per row and verified by an observed-plus-S run, as in review round 2; used is the leaves of one proof and used_incomplete when it rests on NAF; sensitivity (monotone, over, defaults) is judged on the desugared program. Open for the owner: whether the oracle should also render procedures and check traces (the optional part, not built).

author: vrc-sopr-agent
title: What came from VRC and sop-r: four components, measured
body: vrc-compressed-planning: exact-rational BFS with certified compression reproduces VRC's state counts (energy 68,726 to 6,313, product 144,799 to 264), 44x and about 1,700x warm, 2.2x and 5.5x cold; the guard-rich control certifies the identity encoding and loses once learning is counted. worlds-sopr: sop-r's 1,200-answer incremental test passes on the vendored engine and 1,200 core answers equal the oracle's; addition worlds 0.24 ms, retraction 3.6 ms, set 7.7 ms at 4,000 entities (not incremental). dreaming-session wrapper: certified join-order skills cut probes 10x to 52x and wall clock 2x to 6x on a repeated family; the dream pass pays back after 9 to 32 queries; a well-ordered control only pays overhead; a sound lemma is rejected on cost (as in E10); the gate is only as strong as its replay tasks. closure-template: 55x to 1,100x against the oracle on reach shapes, 120 random programs equal to the oracle. Numeric cases 70-73 wait for the grammar import of sop/knowledge/numeric-action.mjs.

author: datalog-agent
title: Datalog strategies: souffle, E10 and soplab as product strategies, shadow clean, measured
body: datalog-souffle (Souffle 2.5), datalog-e10 and datalog-soplab (zip engines vendored verbatim) share one host front end and the oracle's query reader. Smoke: souffle 61, e10 56, soplab 65 passes, 0 fails (108 cases); cases 65-69 pass on the oracle and all three. Differential fuzz against the oracle, 300 seeds, ~20k answers, 0 disagreements (Souffle with magic sets too). Findings: soplab native abduct() is cheapest-only (strategy enumerates all minimal); sop/knowledge/lexical.mjs parse() is quadratic (50k wires 10.8 s), so large inputs go as structured wires; private Souffle compile mode works with CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH=install/include; Souffle provenance not wired. Speed at 10^6 ring facts: souffle 6.4 s (3.3 s magic), e10 7.5 s demand / 65 s without, sql-sqlite 28.7 s; E10 demand loses on dense nonlinear recursion (1.9 s vs 0.9 s at 100 nodes). Oracle is probe-bound already at 10^3 facts.

author: solver-agent
title: asp-clingo and z3-smt-bounded: what the solvers add, and where they stop
body: Both strategies pass every smoke case they declare against js-oracle (asp-clingo 88, z3-smt-bounded 74 of 131; zero disagreements) and agree with each other on norm scenarios. What they add: abduction with all minimal sets and why_not as choice plus minimize; bounded planning with norms as violation atoms and a lifted no-violation requirement that names blockers (stages A, B, C), including a deontic conflict of equal strength; optimisation with the oracle's tie order. Findings: (1) gringo integers are 32 bits and wrap silently (2000000000*2 gives -294967296), so an overflow guard was needed: witness rules for compute, a range check on sums, wide constants not_expressible; (2) bare 'true' in a clingo body is an undefined atom, '#true' is the literal; (3) a min or max written as a nested ite that repeats its operand is exponential in size, a let chain is linear (case 51, 2500 members); (4) unsat within a horizon cannot be no_plan, but for Markov norms an unsat search plus an unsat search for a loopless path of H actions proves it, and a cost bound (H+1 times the cheapest action) certifies the optimum; (5) completion fails on an unfounded loop (probe z3-64-unfounded-loop.smt2), so recursion stays not_expressible for Z3. Limits: no proofs (explain not declared), no budget/budget_probes features, why_not is minimum-cardinality where the oracle is inclusion-minimal over the nearest explanation, clingo does not order time texts. Speed on the smoke cases: 5 to 130 ms per question for clingo, 13 to 220 ms for Z3 (case 51 with 4000 facts: 132 and 223 ms); the full 131-case table takes about 13 s for clingo and 5 s for Z3 against 2 s for the oracle.

author: planner-agent
title: conform lowering and htn-strips-planner: results, shadows and findings
body:
Result of the first two strategies of the owner's build order (planner-agent, 2026-10-01). Scope: `reasoning/strategies/modes/`, `conform/`, `htn-strips-planner/`; cases 40a to 49d.

**Conform lowered to core rules.** A trace plus the norms and methods in force at the time of its steps become one core program (predicate, fact and rule wires). It gives the same verdict as the planner's own monitors on 9,600 generated traces over eight domains (0 disagreements), and the same verdict as the oracle on prolog-tabling, datalog-souffle, sql-sqlite, asp-clingo and z3-smt-bounded for the smoke traces; E10 and soplab refuse it (no arithmetic). The oracle is wrapped, not rewritten; the only change in it is the default `binding strict` in its policy reader.

**htn-strips-planner.** Passes 11a-c and 30a-39b (35c and 35d stay with the oracle) and the 23 new cases. Shadows: 300 generated road graphs give the oracle's status and plan cost; 276 generated norm problems (cost mutations, severity flips, deadlines) give the cost of an exhaustive search judged by the same monitors; 300 method plans re-checked by conform are compliant at the same cost. Speed: a 6x6 road grid in 29 ms (the oracle: 4.1 s), 10x10 in 0.1 s (the oracle gives up after 30 s). The first version expanded 10,749 nodes on 6x6 because an open fluent that moves records negative literals and every path became a new state; deduplicating on the negative literals somebody reads fixed it.

**Findings about the earlier cases.** 30d expected `supported`, but section 5.3 gives `hypotheses` as the status of an abduction; 32 declared open valve predicates and `requires not`, which has no evidence by 4.2 item 8, so the case as written had no plan; both corrected in their READMEs. The oracle's `selectInForce` once excluded a contested wire (now fixed upstream in `sop/knowledge/governance.mjs`). The harness's `lib/conditional.mjs` ignored a governed wire or amendment supposed with `if`, so 30c and 36 could never pass; fixed.

**Decisions taken where the proposal is silent** (all in DS006): a norm instance is violated once, at its first step; relevance of an obligation's binding includes the next step's parameters; an unmet obligation at the end of the run is a violation; the state tested in a method's `if` is the one right after the last consumed step of its scope; a method is engaged by an instance taken from a step that performs one of its primitives; `within N` counts days in a fully timestamped trace; only a forbid of an action can be overridden.

author: agent
title: prolog-tabling and golog-swi: results, shadows and the call_with_time_limit finding
body: prolog-tabling (SWI tabling, private 9.0.4): two tabled predicates per relation, tnot for absent, goal-directed queries, proofs from a tabled height variant (min mode), why_not by an abductive meta-interpreter, all-minimal abduction, maxJoins by inference limit, maxRounds by the height encoding. Passes the 82 smoke cases it declares; shadow against the oracle: every declared case equal (one difference: a probe cut returns no partial rows, the oracle a prefix), 600 random programs and the nine VRC tabled files (row counts equal to SWI) with zero disagreements; well-founded undefined maps to unknown (tested on a hand-built non-stratified program, the compiler refuses such programs). Finding: call_with_time_limit deadlocks SWI 9.0.4 at halt (1 hang in about 1700 runs with the alarm, 0 in 10500 without), so the wall limit is a process kill. golog-swi: methods as Golog programs, norms as tests over complete runs, plan through methods, conform and strict-method deviation, why_not via, abduce waive, procedure; passes the 31 cases it declares and agrees with the htn-strips-planner on all 31 shared cases and 16 scenario programs. Not covered: blind planning, relational modes. New cases 55-58 (prolog-tabling) and 59a, 59b (golog).

author: sql-agent
title: sql-sqlite: 71 smoke cases agree with the oracle, fuzz 0 disagreements, speed and limits
body: All smoke cases sql-sqlite declares (71) pass; 2,500 fuzz seeds (incl. intervals, start_of/end_of, nonlinear/mutual recursion) agree with js-oracle with used replayed. Nonlinear and mutual recursion are lowered by a semi-naive loop over SQL statements (not declared out). Rules are materialised per stratum, not views. Bank mode (askBank) is read-only, byte-identical file after runs, uses the bank indexes. Speed (loaded machine, ratios only): 3-way join 3.2e5 facts 2.2 s vs E10 5.4 s; policy NAF 1.8e5 facts 2.2 s vs 13 s; aggregates 4e5 3.6 s vs oracle 10 s; E10 wins small mutual recursion and right-linear bound closures (magic sets). Oracle findings: every+both is first-binding dependent; oracle used for start_of names the first fact of the tuple (case: on c valid 2026-01-01 2026-02-01 and on c timeless, rule began x s from start_of, query began c beginning: used [r,t0] replays to unknown); oracle timeoutMs only checked at probes.

author: llm-strategy-agent
title: llm-agent baseline: first LLM-through-omp agreement with the oracle (Grok, GLM), cases 80-84
body: Strategy llm-agent (advisory: exact false, bounded false, verified false) runs a model through omp --no-tools in a temp folder; strict JSON parse, cache, cost from usage events, verify by oracle replay. Smoke, 136 cases (50, 51, 54 exceed the prompt limit), answer-content agreement with the oracle: Grok non-reasoning sop 74% (101/136), Grok reasoning sop 91% (124/136); on the 47 cases with a source.md: nl 85% (non-reasoning), 94% (Grok reasoning), 94% (GLM glm-5.3-flash); sop on the same 47: 83%, 94%, 91%. JSON-only replies scored 52% for the non-reasoning model, so the default is work-through-then-JSON. Failures: planning with norms (35/52 and 49/52), not vs absent (05c), partly covered time (12e), why-not over unknown, budget honesty 1/6 (an LLM cannot know an engine budget ran out). New cases 80-84: reasoning models solve 80, 82, 84 at 30-60 facts, the non-reasoning model fails 80, 83, 84; a scale probe of case 80 at 60, 150 and 400 nodes breaks Grok reasoning at every size (it misses the one missing link) and GLM at 150. Verify mode: 70 of 71 verified Grok-reasoning answers are right. Cost: paid 0 USD (subscription models); notional about 4 USD for the table. Honest limits: small easy smoke, oracle defines the answer, one run per configuration, prompt iterated once on formatting. Recommended harder families are in the report (scale, absence, deep recursion with negation, many-worlds, numeric planning, compile-from-text, budget parity).

author: retire-agent
title: Old JavaScript reasoner retired; oracle is the reference route (32,082 corpus calls identical)
body:
**Result.** The retired JavaScript reasoner (`reasoning/reasoner.mjs`, with `solvers.mjs`, `backends/`, `optimization.mjs`) is gone; the oracle `js-reference` is the `reference` route through `reasoning/bridge/`.

**Method.** Before deleting, the old `reason` and the bridge answered the same 32,082 runtime Horn calls of the real corpora (formalizer-v1 sealed test 10,858, dev 10,978, train slice 6,466, ood 3,780; kinds exists, select, count, every, explain, with time variables, compares, quantifiers and assumptions). Compared fields: status, answers with validity, count, conflicted answers, proof (ids, kinds, rules, premises, atoms, validity), depth, explanation, members, counterexamples, undecided, defeated assumptions, complete, truncated. Result: 0 differences. Two defects were found and fixed on the way: a partial positive answer (`complete: false`, not `budget_exhausted`) was read as complete, and rows found part by part were listed in chronological instead of fact order.

**Inventory (feature, user, status).** closure with budgets and blocked heads (runtime, controllers, qualification): covered, `bridge/closure.mjs` over `saturate`. select, exists, count, explain with proof, depth, derived-fact ids (chat, eval, corpora): covered by `bridge/reason.mjs`. every with `all|none|not_all|most|half|at_least` (chat, corpora, query-forms tests): ported to `js-reference/forms.mjs`. compare, rank, except, filter, limit, numeric coercion, not_computable (chat, corpora): ported. at, during, answers with validity, `mixed_temporal`, span, measure, order (chat, corpora, temporal tests): in the bridge, one oracle call per validity part. assumptions, `hypothetical`, defeated (chat, tests): bridge. abduce, diagnose, associate, induce, analogize, plan, simulate (docs examples, tests, examples/reasoning, no chat or corpus user): the controllers stay and run over the oracle's closure; the oracle's native abduce and plan keep their own packets (owner decides later whether to converge). constraint and optimize, js (runtime, docs): ported to `constraint-ast.mjs`. backend prolog: `prolog-tabling` checked against the oracle. backend z3: `z3-smt-bounded/ast.mjs`. compile-smt and compile-prolog (CLI, demo): `bridge/export.mjs`. `retrieve`, `requiredPredicates`: no user, dropped.

**Open for the owner.** `advanced` is deprecated but kept; whether the controllers should converge on the oracle's own abduce and plan packets; the oracle's `time` versus `wall` reason (kept `time`).

author: agent
title: Linking proposal adopted; M0+M1 started

author: slice-path-agent
title: Slice path: demand-driven keyed retrieval, settled slices, and the two answer paths
body: Decided by principle (correct, generic, no hack). (a) Facts are retrieved by keyed lookups driven by a static magic-set style plan (sideways information passing, head positions seeded only when every call site binds them, scans only for atoms no constant reaches) plus a run-time value domain per variable class; completeness is proven by the fixpoint of that demand, not by hop counts. (b) A slice is complete (fixpoint, no truncation, rules complete, no budget stop) and settled (also exact: R-P3). Only a settled slice supports count, a universal answer that no counterexample decided, a ranking or a failure-derived unknown; they are widened and otherwise withheld as incomplete with partial_retrieval and a lower bound. (c) Monotone positives (exists/explain proofs, counterexamples) are accepted over a partial slice and flagged. (d) The typed runtime has no negation as failure or defaults, so those are judged on the knowledge-wire path from the oracle sensitivity. (e) closedWorld stays view by default on the chat path (counts and every over a complete exact view are the memory's world) and is declared on the wire path (the oracle reads the predicate closed flags); this keeps user-stated counts exact. Alternative rejected: hop expansion from the question constants (over-fetches a hub and cannot tell a disconnected body atom).

author: slice-path-agent
title: Slice path measured: world-v1 chat latency and synthetic scale
body: Acceptance (tools/linking/acceptance-chat.mjs, private port): Ada 162.7 s -> 19-21 s (fresh server), Paris city 92.3 -> 0.8-1.0 s, Paris where 89.3 -> 0.9-1.1 s; the first-question cost is 12 s SymbolicLM start (same on the empty default base) plus 3.9 s to decode the 219-snapshot chain once per process (it was 9.7 s per lookup). Synthetic SQLite memories (tools/eval/slice-timing.mjs, CPU): keyed lookup 7/44/142 ms, two-hop join 8/48/157 ms, recursive ancestor 9/50/183 ms, hub select 27/121/287 ms, hub every 100/1401/3857 ms at 10k/100k/300k facts; a count over a 50k-fact relation is incomplete under the 10k fact budget. Cause found on the way: a session over a base memory built circuit by circuit walked its snapshot chain through a 16-entry cache on every recall.

author: router-agent
title: StrategyRouter v1: design and rules (router-agent's own choices)
body: Wire-level router in reasoning/router/ (features read from the same compiled program as the engines; engines.mjs: availability + eligibility from declared capabilities; index.mjs: decide + routedAsk + verification). Rules: proof/mode-of-work/host forms/caller budget -> oracle; small slice -> oracle (thresholds nonlinear 100, recursion 300, other 10000 facts, from the measured table); scale -> linear recursion SQLite then Soufflé then clingo, everything else Soufflé then SQLite then clingo; verification by the oracle always up to 20000 facts, else a deterministic 1/8 sample, discrepancy returns the oracle answer. Integrated in askMemory (default auto) and POST /v1/sessions/{id}/query (reasoning, verify); typed path 'auto' reports the oracle route. Explicit ids never substituted. clingo is in the order but never wins on the measured classes.

author: router-agent
title: StrategyRouter v1 measured: 140/140 smoke agreement, 17/17 scale cells correct
body: Smoke arm 140 of 140 agree (67 routed to engines). Scale arm: router complete and correct on 17 of 17 cells, oracle alone complete on 8 of 17. At 10^5 facts negation 866 vs 399 ms, aggregates 1262 vs 414 ms, linear recursion 721 (incomplete) vs 418 ms; at 10^4 verification makes the router slower (139 vs 207 ms). Slice arm: 13 of 14 runs stay on the oracle (small slices), 14 of 14 agree. Verification is 'unverified' on large closures because the oracle exhausts its own budget.

author: omp-t2-engine
title: T2 engine query forms
body: SQLite already computes demand-driven closures and joins; reuse the oracle forms evaluator on full SQL join bindings rather than copy semantics or rerun recursive closure. Verification must be independent of execution budget and offline replay must disclose unresolved oracle budgets.

author: omp-t3-bench
title: Evidence renderer and completion contract
body: Render Theory and gold slices without discarding negative, default, closed, temporal, or aggregate semantics; completion backend must preserve model selection and failure provenance.

author: omp-t2-engine
title: Planning slice joins exclude future transitions
body: Focused planning scenario in recall-memory sharded repository yields no_plan with only located_in robot_0 place_a_0 and connected place_a_0 place_b_0 in request.memory. Runtime at sop/runtime.mjs:168-175 constructs one conjunctive retrieval query from goal plus every action requires; demand binds connected ?from ?to to initial located_in ?r ?from and never asks connected place_b_0 place_c_0, despite direct repo.recall keyed place_b_0 retrieving that road complete=true. This is a planning retrieval-demand contract error, not loss in RecallMemory. Correct query must explicitly represent independent future-state/static-action demands; definite no_plan must remain withheld on incomplete retrieval.

author: omp-t4-latency
title: T4 latency profile and independent fixes
body: Profile world-v1 query-form and F1 dev rows with retrieval, SQLite, engine and verification timing; preserve answer projections and completeness guards. Planning prerequisite retrieval and opt-in self-check implemented independently within owned files.

author: omp-t4-latency
title: Planning retrieval uses independent future-state demands
body: In sop/runtime.mjs planning unlinks goal, action requirements, and selected rule bodies before retrieval, retaining KnowledgeLinker budgets and rule-closure bounds. A negative no_plan over a partial or inexact slice is withheld as budget_exhausted/partial_retrieval. Scoped regression covers two-step planning, rule-dependent reachability, read-only execution and a fact cap.

author: omp-t4-latency
title: Converse recursion loses retrieval keys
body: World-v1 contains mutually recursive located_in/contains rules. The previous static common-bound-position plan cannot propagate a key through the converse dependency cycle, so it scans relations. Directed rule instances per lookup position retain recursive inputs and avoid unrelated hub members; a real Europe ranking returned Russia with a settled 806-fact slice, rather than about 40k facts. Initial profile script failed on indentation and was corrected; baseline profile remains running.

author: omp-t4-latency
title: Stored counts are optimistic for derived relations
body: An unrestricted base-cardinality tie-break improved scoped city rankings but regressed Europe ranking from an 806-fact slice to 14,056 facts (19.4 s), because a small number of direct Europe edges hides derived fanout. Retained directed demand and added a conservative twelve-fold estimate margin whenever either tied predicate has rule producers; estimates affect ordering only, never completeness. Final measurements pending. The actual planning scenario passes with cost 2 and unchanged session revision on all five memory engines. Full npm test still fails only on concurrent T5 report-directory cleanup, outside ownership.

author: omp-t4-latency
title: T4 bound-prefix priority and conservative selectivity
body: Raw stored cardinalities understated recursive located_in fanout and initially moved global country classes into bound multi-hop paths. Final ordering prioritizes bound variables before constant-only ties and requires an eight-fold estimate advantage for predicates with producers: country/Europe ratio 3.94 retains written order, city/Japan ratio 8.62 selects the scoped lookup. Estimates are cost hints only. Final deterministic 500-graph-answer differential smoke has zero disagreements; focused suite 77 passed, one existing Berlin-population skip, no failures in 36.43 seconds. Paired 35-row values are unchanged; 14 packets now report complete retrieval, including one former incomplete ranking. Default-parallel npm test passed 1217, skipped one, cancelled site-links at its unchanged 120-second deadline; bounded concurrency rerun preserves all tests and timeouts.

author: owner
title: Three formalization strategies: CodingAgent, LocalLLMDirect, LocalLLMStepByStep
body: Owner, 2026-10-02: "la modele mici de genul 4B nu am putea pune simbolic mai multe întrebări și să scoatem noi circuitul SOP Lang pas cu pas din răspunsuri, să nu mai dea nici un JSON sau SOP Lang, ci poate o listă sau markdown, dar îl folosim ca un oracol ce ne ajută să identificăm relații, constrângeri … întâi să punem întrebări high level să identificăm despre cine se fac afirmații, despre ce cereri, care sunt entitățile importante. Fă aici ca un fel de strategie de formalizare separată alături de LocalLLMDirect, Coding Agent, să avem un LocalLLMStepByStep". Also agreed: solve the vocabulary problem by symbolic detection and a bounded dialog (schema neighbourhood of the question's entities, examples, definitions in the session), without sending the whole memory.
